extracted.intended_audience: research mathematicians and advanced graduate students specializing in arithmetic geometry, anabelian geometry, and Mochizuki's inter-universal Teichmüller theory (IUT)
extracted.subtask_description: Definitions, structural requirements, and group-theoretic reconstruction/rigidity criteria for mono-theta (and related bi-theta) environments and for elementary/model Frobenioids appearing in IUT; includes algorithmic reconstructability statements and rigidity properties used to recognize and recover geometric data from group-theoretic inputs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mod N model mono-theta environment (Definition 7.20)
rubrics_metrics.description: A mod N model mono-theta environment consists of: (i) the topological group π_temp[Y][(Z/NZ)]; (ii) the subgroup DY (a subgroup of Out(π_temp[Y][(Z/NZ)])); (iii) the (Z/NZ)-conjugacy class of subgroups in π_temp[Y][(Z/NZ)]; and the theta section s_Θ^Y determined by the image of (the displayed theta object).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This lists the concrete data attached to the model coming from a chosen member of the theta class; the mod N model is the template to which abstract mod N mono-theta environments should be compared (see below for the general notion and isomorphism notion).

rubrics_metrics.name: Mod N mono-theta environment (abstract) (Definition 7.20 (2))
rubrics_metrics.description: A mod N mono-theta environment M = (π; D(π); s_Θ(π)) is: (a) a topological group π; (b) a subgroup D(π) ⊂ Out(π); and (c) a collection of subgroups s_Θ(π) of π, such that there exists an isomorphism of topological groups mapping these data to the model data (π_temp[Y][(Z/NZ)], DY, the (Z/NZ)-conjugacy class determined by the theta section).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An abstract environment qualifies only if it can be identified (via an isomorphism of topological groups) with the mod N model environment; the existence of such an isomorphism is part of the definition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Isomorphism / homomorphism of mod N mono-theta environments (Definition 7.20 (3))
rubrics_metrics.description: An isomorphism of mod N mono-theta environments M -> M' is an isomorphism of the underlying topological groups mapping D(π) to D'(π) and carrying the theta-section conjugacy classes appropriately; for M and M' with M' at a divisor M | N, a homomorphism is the induced isomorphism to the mod M environment coming from M.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This defines the morphisms in the category of mono-theta environments and the compatibility when passing from mod N to mod M (M | N); precise mapping conditions for subgroups and theta-section conjugacy classes must be satisfied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bi-theta environment datum (Remark 7.20.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: A mod N bi-theta environment B = (π; D(π); s_Θ(π); s_alg(π)) includes, in addition to the mono-theta data, a datum s_alg corresponding to the (Z/NZ)-conjugacy class of the image of a mod N algebraic section s_alg.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bi-theta environments include the algebraic section as part of the input data; as noted, some rigidities (cyclotomic and constant-multiple) trivially hold for bi-theta environments whereas discrete rigidity may fail. The text omits full bi-theta details because they are not used further in the survey.

rubrics_metrics.name: Group-theoretic characterization of image of tautological section (Lemma 7.21 (1))
rubrics_metrics.description: The image of the tautological section of π_1^temp(Y) [(Z/NZ)] as a subgroup of π_1^temp(Y) [(Z/NZ)] is described as the intersection of elements a in π_1^temp(Y) [(Z/NZ)] satisfying: the image of the corresponding lift in Out(π_temp[Y][(Z/NZ)]) belongs to DY, and the lift induces the identity on the quotient π_temp[Y] -> π_temp[Y]/(kernel) (and on GK).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This gives a concrete, group-theoretic criterion to recognize which subgroup of the tempered fundamental group arises from the tautological theta section—used in reconstruction arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Existence of conjugate section and associated 1-cocycle (Lemma 7.21 (2))
rubrics_metrics.description: Given the theta section s_Θ^Y, there exists a conjugate section t_Θ^Y obtained by conjugation by some element; the conjugation difference is a 1-cocycle of π_temp[Y][(Z/NZ)] valued in the N-torsion giving identity on both the quotient and the kernel, and this 1-cocycle extends to an automorphism preserving DY and inducing identity on the appropriate quotients.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This describes the 'shifting automorphisms' phenomenon: conjugating the theta section yields cocycles valued in the finite torsion, and these conjugations preserve the structural subgroup DY and act trivially on quotients—important for understanding automorphism ambiguity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Automorphism action on a mod N model (Lemma 7.21 (3))
rubrics_metrics.description: Every automorphism of the mod N model mono-theta environment M induces an automorphism of π_temp^Y and of the set of cusps of Y; via the labelling by Z this yields an automorphism of Z given by (Z_l) ∘ f, producing a surjective homomorphism Aut(M) -> (Z_l) ∘ f (image of DY -> Out(π_temp^Y)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Automorphisms of the environment are tightly controlled and factor through automorphisms of the fundamental group and the cuspidal data; this statement underlies later counts of automorphism fibers and torsors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Group-theoretic reconstruction of mono-theta environment (Corollary 7.22 (1))
rubrics_metrics.description: From a topological group yπ_temp^X isomorphic to π_temp^X, there is a group-theoretic algorithm to construct subquotients yπ_temp^Y, yGK, y(l^*), and a collection of subgroups of yπ_temp^X indexed by (Z/lZ)/{±1}, such that any isomorphism to the original π_temp^X maps these reconstructed subquotients and subgroup collections to the canonical ones functorially (no reference isomorphism needed).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an explicit reconstructibility criterion: the tempered fundamental group alone suffices (algorithmically) to recover the key subquotients and cuspidal decomposition groups and labels in a functorial manner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Construction of mod N mono-theta environment from π_temp^X (Corollary 7.22 (2))
rubrics_metrics.description: There exists a group-theoretic algorithm that, given yπ_temp^X, constructs (up to isomorphism, functorially) a mod N mono-theta environment yM = (yπ; Dy; s_Θ(yπ)) isomorphic to the model MN (independent of choices up to specified identity).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This provides a criterion for producing the full environment from the group: from the tempered fundamental group one can algorithmically build the mono-theta environment, i.e., the environment is a group-theoretic invariant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reconstruction of quotient and functoriality for environments (Corollary 7.22 (3))
rubrics_metrics.description: Given a mod N mono-theta environment yM isomorphic to MN, there is an algorithmic construction of a quotient yπ such that any isomorphism yM -> MN maps this quotient to the canonical quotient π_temp[Y][(Z/NZ)]; further, applying the algorithm of (2) to yπ recovers yM via an isomorphism inducing the identity on yπ_temp^Y.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This gives a two-way reconstructibility and consistency check: from the environment one recovers the quotient tempered group and back, with functorial behavior under isomorphisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Isomorphism maps and fiber cardinality in reconstruction (Corollary 7.22 (4))
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a natural surjective map Isom_{(Z/NZ)-conj}(yM, zM) -> Isom(yπ_temp^X, zπ_temp^X) whose fibers have cardinality 1 if N odd and 2 if N even; similarly natural homomorphisms between automorphism groups for varying moduli M | N with kernel described as Hom(yπ_temp^Y / yπ_temp^{Y,(1)}, ker(yπ -> yπ_temp^Y)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This quantifies the ambiguity in lifting isomorphisms of the reconstructed tempered groups to isomorphisms of the mono-theta environments and gives explicit torsor descriptions and parity dependence on N.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cyclotomic rigidity of mono-theta environments (Theorem 7.23 (1))
rubrics_metrics.description: For yM isomorphic to the model MN, there is a group-theoretic algorithm to construct subquotients y(l^*)([Z/NZ]) and y(((π_temp^1)(2))[Z/NZ]) etc., and two splittings of the surjection y(l^*( )[Z/NZ]) -> y(l^* ), such that any isomorphism to MN maps these to the algebraic and theta-derived splittings; taking their difference yields a canonical isomorphism of cyclotomes y(l^*) ⊗ Z/NZ -> (Z/NZ)(y(l^*[Z/NZ])) preserved functorially.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cyclotomic rigidity says the cyclotome (the cyclotomic-like torsor object) can be reconstructed group-theoretically and is rigid under isomorphisms of environments; the construction uses both the algebraic and theta sections and their splittings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discrete rigidity of mono-theta environments (Theorem 7.23 (2))
rubrics_metrics.description: Any projective system (y_{M,N})_N of mono-theta environments is isomorphic to the natural projective system of the model mono-theta environments (M_N)_N.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discrete rigidity asserts uniqueness of the projective system: as N varies, the compatible system of mod N environments is determined (no extra continuous ambiguity), relying on vanishing R^1 lim terms in the relevant torsion inverse systems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Constant multiple rigidity (Theorem 7.23 (3))
rubrics_metrics.description: Under standard-type assumptions on the theta class set, for any projective system of mono-theta environments (y_{M,N}) there is a group-theoretic algorithm producing a collection of H^1-classes so that any isomorphism to the model projective system maps these classes to the corresponding model H^1-classes up to multiplication by an element of Z_l (i.e., a constant multiple) functorially.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This rigidifies the ambiguity of cohomology classes arising from theta functions: although an overall Z_l-multiple may remain, the collection is determined up to that global multiple, and the statement depends on previous lemmas (elliptic cuspidalisation, cyclotomic/discrete rigidity).

rubrics_metrics.name: Orbicurve of type (1; l-tors) (Definition 7.24)
rubrics_metrics.description: An orbicurve over K is of type (1; l-tors) if it is isomorphic over K to some X^0! obtained from a hyperbolic curve X of type (1;1) and choice of cusp data and a prime l as constructed (X^0! is the covering with Gal(X^0!/X) = (I_α) ≅ Z/lZ determined by the chosen torsor data).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This identifies the special cover X^0! (with ordered cuspidal orbit direction indicated by the arrow) as the canonical object used to play the role of X at good places in IUT; the precise construction involves quotienting by the image of a section to a profinite extension J_X.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reconstructibility from X^0! (Lemma 7.25)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assuming K is NF or MLF, from π_{X^0!}^temp one can group-theoretically reconstruct π_X and π_C (as subgroups of Aut(X^0!)) together with conjugacy classes of decomposition groups determined by specified cusps; one can also recover l (via index formulas), and the reconstructed groups are slim and characterized functorially.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a concrete reconstruction criterion: the cover X^0! contains enough group-theoretic information to recover the original curve X, the orbicurve C, the cuspidal decomposition classes, and the prime l used in the torsion cover, with uniqueness conditions at l≥5 used in splitting characterizations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Elementary Frobenioid structure (Definition 8.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given a monoid-valued contravariant functor Θ: D -> Mon (a monoid on D), the elementary Frobenioid F(Θ) is the category with objects Ob(D) and for A,B in Ob(D) Hom_{F(Θ)}(A,B) the set of triples φ = (Base(φ); Div(φ); degFr(φ)) with Base(φ) ∈ Hom_D(A,B), Div(φ) ∈ Θ(A), and degFr(φ) ∈ N_{≥1}; composition is defined by the displayed formula combining Base, Div, and multiplicative degrees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: F(Θ) packages base morphisms, divisor data from Θ, and a Frobenius-degree parameter into morphisms; there is a natural functor F(Θ) -> D and induced operations Base, Div, degFr on any pre-Frobenioid C receiving a functor to F(Θ). Definitions of O^2(A) (automorphisms with Base=id and degFr=1) and O^3(A) (endomorphisms with Base=id and degFr=1) are given, as are torsion subsets (Z/NZ)(A).

rubrics_metrics.name: Split pre-Frobenioid criterion (Definition 8.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: A pre-Frobenioid C equipped with a functorial splitting spl: O^3/O^2 -> O^3 (or a (Z/NZ)-orbit of such functorial splittings for fixed N) is called a split pre-Frobenioid (resp. a (Z/NZ)-split pre-Frobenioid).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Existence of such functorial splittings (or orbits thereof) of the local endomorphism quotient by automorphisms is the structural datum of splitting used to define split pre-Frobenioids; practical uses appear in model Frobenioid constructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Model Frobenioid prerequisites and object description (Definition 8.3 start)
rubrics_metrics.description: A model Frobenioid is built from a monoid Θ: D -> Mon together with a group-like monoid B: D -> Mon and a homomorphism Div_B: B -> Θ^{gp}; setting Θ^{birat} := Im(Div_B), one forms a category C whose objects are pairs A = (A_D; ψ) with A_D ∈ Ob(D) and ψ ∈ Θ(A_D)^{gp}; morphisms are then defined (definition continued) using the base category, divisor monoid and degree data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This entry records the required inputs and object form for constructing model Frobenioids: a divisor monoid Θ, an auxiliary group-like monoid B and a divisor map; the formal morphism rules follow and define the Frobenioid structure used in IUT (see [FrdI, Theorem 5.2]).
